focus: 'It was X that...' cleft stress · 'What I need is...' cleft build-up · 'so ... that' / 'such a ... that' · emphatic 'do/did' · contrastive stress shifting
focus_ar: نبر 'It was X that...'، وبناء 'What I need is...'، و'so...that' و'such a...that'، والتوكيد بـ do/did، ونقل النبر التقابلي
arabic_challenge: English creates emphasis by RESTRUCTURING the sentence and moving the main stress, whereas Arabic often adds words (إنّ، فعلاً) or changes word order more freely. Learners who translate directly produce correct-but-flat English and can't highlight the point they care about.

target_sounds: 'It was X that...' cleft — stress the highlighted element

isolation.instructions: This structure spotlights ONE element and it takes the main stress: 'It was SARA that called' (not someone else). Everything after 'that' drops in pitch — it's already-known information.
isolation.instructions_ar: هذا التركيب يسلّط الضوء على عنصر واحد يأخذ النبر الرئيسي: 'It was SARA that called'. وما بعد 'that' يهبط.
practice: It was YESterday that we met

pair: It was yesterday that we met
It wasn't me that did it

word_practice: it was yesterday that we met
it was here that it happened
it was John who told me
it wasn't me that did it
it was then that I realised
it was the noise that woke me

sentence_practice: It was Sara that called, not Mona.
It was yesterday that we met, not today.
It wasn't me that broke it.
daily_drills.record_this: It was Sara that called me last night, not Mona. It was yesterday that we met at the café, not today. Honestly, it wasn't me that broke the window.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'It was SARA that called.' Is the main stress on 'SARA', with everything after 'that' lower?

target_sounds: 'What I need is...' cleft — build-up then landing

isolation.instructions: This structure builds suspense: say 'What I really need is...' fairly flat and slightly rising, then LAND hard on the key word: 'What I need is a HOLiday.' The delay creates the emphasis.
isolation.instructions_ar: هذا التركيب يبني تشويقًا: قل 'What I really need is...' بنبرة مسطحة صاعدة قليلاً، ثم انزل بقوة على الكلمة المفتاح.
practice: What I need is ... ə HOLiday
What surprised me was ... the PRICE

pair: What I need is a HOLiday

sentence_practice: What I really need is a holiday.
What surprised me was the price.
All I want is a quiet evening.
daily_drills.record_this: What I really need right now is a proper holiday. What genuinely surprised me was the price of the tickets. All I want this evening is a quiet cup of tea.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'What I need is a HOLiday.' Did the first part stay flat before landing hard on 'HOLiday'?

isolation.instructions: Both intensify, and the ADJECTIVE stretches: 'It was sooo COLD that the pipes froze.' Use 'so + adjective' and 'such a + adjective + noun'. Lengthening the vowel is what carries the intensity.
isolation.instructions_ar: كلتاهما للتكثيف، والصفة تُمدّ: 'It was sooo COLD that...'. استخدم 'so + صفة' و'such a + صفة + اسم'.

sentence_practice: It was so cold that the pipes froze.
It was such a long day that I fell asleep.
There was so much noise that I couldn't think.
daily_drills.record_this: It was so cold last night that the pipes actually froze. It had been such a long day that I fell asleep on the sofa. There was so much noise outside that I simply couldn't think.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'It was so cold that the pipes froze.' Did you stretch 'cold' to carry the intensity?

isolation.instructions: Add a stressed auxiliary to insist or contradict: 'I DID tell you!', 'I DO like it!' Normally there's no auxiliary in positive statements — adding one is pure emphasis, and it must be stressed.
isolation.instructions_ar: أضف مساعدًا منبورًا للإصرار أو التصحيح: 'I DID tell you!'. عادة لا يوجد مساعد في المثبت، فوجوده توكيد خالص.

sentence_practice: I did tell you — you weren't listening!
daily_drills.record_this: I did tell you about it — you simply weren't listening! I do like it, honestly, I'm not just being polite. She does care about you, even if she doesn't say so.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'I DID tell you!' Is the auxiliary clearly stressed so it sounds like insistence?

isolation.instructions: Move the stress to change the meaning without changing a word: 'I didn't say HE stole it' (someone else did) vs 'I didn't SAY he stole it' (I implied it). Practise moving the stress deliberately.
isolation.instructions_ar: انقل النبر لتغيّر المعنى بدون تغيير الكلمات: 'I didn't say HE stole it' مقابل 'I didn't SAY he stole it'.
practice: I didn't say HE stole it
I didn't SAY he stole it

pair: I didn't say HE stole it

word_practice: I didn't say HE stole it
I didn't SAY he stole it
sentence_practice: I didn't say HE stole it.
I didn't SAY he stole it.
daily_drills.record_this: I didn't say HE stole it — I said somebody stole it. Actually, I didn't SAY he stole it; I only suggested it. That's honestly not what I MEANT at all.
daily_drills.self_check: Say the same sentence three times with the stress in different places. Does the meaning genuinely change each time?

daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: main stress on the spotlighted element, build-up before landing, and stressed emphatic 'do/did'.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself correcting a misunderstanding and insisting on your version. Emphasis structures only work if the stress is right, so listen closely to WHERE your stress falls.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك تصحّح سوء فهم وتصرّ على روايتك. تراكيب التوكيد لا تعمل إلا بنبر صحيح، فاسمع أين يقع نبرك.
test_yourself.passage: Let me set the record straight, because what happened wasn't what people are saying. It was Karim who suggested the change, not me. I did raise concerns at the time — several people heard me. What I actually said was that the timing was risky, whereas the idea itself was fine. The meeting was so rushed that nobody wrote anything down. Consequently, it's now my word against his. What frustrates me most is the assumption that I stayed silent. I didn't stay silent; I was ignored. It was in that meeting that the mistake was made, and it was the rush that caused it. I do understand why people are confused. Nevertheless, what matters now isn't blame — it's fixing the problem before Friday.

sounds_to_check.'It was X that/who' clefts: It was KaRIM who suggested, it was in THAT MEETing that, it was the RUSH that caused it
sounds_to_check.'What...' clefts with build-up: what HAPPened wasn't..., what I ACTually said was..., what FRUStrates me most is..., what MATters now isn't...
sounds_to_check.emphatic 'do/did': I DID raise concerns, I DO understand
sounds_to_check.'so ... that': so RUSHED that nobody wrote anything down
sounds_to_check.contrastive stress: I didn't stay SILent; I was IGnored

scoring_guide.90_100: Emphasis lands exactly where intended; the correction is persuasive. Ready for week 16.
scoring_guide.70_89: Good; occasional stress on the wrong element.
scoring_guide.50_69: Cleft structures used but delivered flat, so no emphasis is heard. Repeat days 1-2 and 5.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, focusing on WHERE the main stress falls in each structure.

for_arabic_speakers: English emphasises by RESTRUCTURING the sentence and moving the main stress, not by adding words.
In 'It was X that...', X takes the main stress and everything after 'that' drops — it is old information.
In 'What I need is...', stay flat through the build-up and land hard on the key word.
'so + adjective' but 'such a + adjective + noun'. Stretch the adjective to carry intensity.
Emphatic 'do/did' only works if you STRESS it — unstressed, it is meaningless.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
